title: Pokémon Turns 30 — and Pikachu's Party Is Still Going
summary:
Happy birthday, Pikachu! Pokémon is 30 years old this year. It all started on February 27, 1996, in Japan, with just two video games. The goal? Catch and train amazing creatures. Now it's the world's most valuable media franchise ever, according to Guinness World Records.

How big is that? Millions of kids and grown-ups play Pokémon games and apps. They also collect the mega-popular Pokémon Trading Card Game, or TCG. The brand has been celebrating all year with in-person events and glossy new cards.

From August 28 to 30, more than 50,000 fans packed the Moscone Center in San Francisco, California, for the 2026 Pokémon World Championships. Players battled for hours in TCG matches. TFK Kid Reporter Adam Sadi was there! He met Haruki Okunishi, a top young player who flew in from Malaysia. Haruki's secret? "I just practice and practice," he said — and it's a lot of fun.

So how does Pokémon stay cool after 30 years? Barry Sams from the Pokémon Company International says it does what Pokémon do best: it evolves. The TCG is now in 16 languages, including Latin American Spanish. One fan said Pokémon "brings together people of all backgrounds and all ages."
why_it_matters: If you have ever traded cards or played a game with friends, you are part of the same idea Pokémon uses: a hobby stays fun for a long time when it keeps changing and when everyone is welcome to join.

background_read: The first Pokémon games came out in Japan for a small handheld game player called the Game Boy, and kids traded creatures with a cable that joined two machines together.

Guinness World Records (a company that keeps track of record-breaking achievements around the world) says Pokémon is the most valuable media franchise — which means it earns more from games, cards, toys and shows than any other brand.
The Pokémon Trading Card Game also started in Japan in the 1990s and then spread around the world, with matches played at card shops, school clubs and big tournaments like the World Championships.
Article_Structure: WHO: Pokémon fans, players and card collectors worldwide, plus TFK Kid Reporter Adam Sadi, young player Haruki Okunishi from Malaysia, and Barry Sams from the Pokémon Company International.
WHAT: Pokémon turns 30, and the 2026 Pokémon World Championships brought more than 50,000 fans together for Trading Card Game battles.
WHERE: The Moscone Center in San Francisco, California — while the brand itself began in Japan on February 27, 1996.
WHY: Pokémon stays popular by 'evolving': the card game is now in 16 languages, including Latin American Spanish, and one fan says it brings together people of all backgrounds and all ages.

perspectives.description: They see 30 years of success and a championship with more than 50,000 fans as proof that the brand is stronger and more popular than ever.
They worry that collecting cards and chasing new games can cost a lot of money and take time away from school, sleep and other hobbies.
For them the fun is in practising, improving and meeting people from other countries who love the same game — not just in winning.
